page: Google Cloud Platform c4a-standard-1 is an entry-tier general-purpose virtual machine built on the 64-bit Arm (arm64) architecture. The instance provides 1 dedicated vCPU paired with 4.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. It operates without integrated local storage, requiring network-attached persistent storage volumes for operating system and application data, and includes no bundled GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Because the single vCPU configuration provides dedicated compute resources rather than a shared or burstable credit model, CPU availability remains predictable under continuous baseline execution. However, with only one core, overall computational throughput is constrained to single-threaded operations or lightly concurrent processes, making scale-up multiprocessing tasks unviable on this machine type.

From an operational cost perspective, this configuration serves as a lightweight, low-footprint deployment target within the Arm ecosystem. It is suited for basic web serving, microservices, continuous integration build runners targeting arm64 architectures, and lightweight background workers.
description: Google Cloud Platform c4a-standard-1 is a general-purpose virtual machine powered by 64-bit Arm (arm64) architecture. Designed as an entry-level instance, it features 1 dedicated vCPU accompanied by 4.0 GB of memory, delivering a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. The configuration includes no local storage or onboard graphics processing units, relying entirely on remote block storage for persistence. Because its single core is dedicated rather than burstable, it offers stable execution metrics without CPU throttling concerns. This makes the c4a-standard-1 resource-efficient for low-load production services, arm64 development pipelines, small proxy services, background task workers, and lightweight container deployments that do not require intense parallel computing capability.
